walkthroughs.body_html:
Quantum & Nuclear Physics — a core area of Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Quantum & Nuclear Physics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Quantum & Nuclear Physics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

How does the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depend on light intensity?
options: It does not — max KE depends only on the frequency of the light; intensity affects the rate (number) of electrons emitted.
Only the total mass in kilograms needs to balance.
Higher intensity gives photoelectrons more kinetic energy.
Intensity has no effect on anything in the photoelectric effect.

mcqs.q: In a balanced nuclear equation, what must be equal on both sides?
options: Only the total mass in kilograms needs to balance.
Only the atomic number (proton count) needs to balance.
The total mass number (top numbers) and the total atomic number (bottom numbers) must both balance.
Gamma rays are slower than X-rays.

mcqs.q: What distinguishes gamma rays from X-rays of the same frequency?
options: Gamma rays have higher frequency than any X-ray.
Origin — gamma rays come from nuclear processes; X-rays come from electron transitions or deceleration of charged particles.
Only the total mass in kilograms needs to balance.
Gamma rays are slower than X-rays.
